d: Record-holding, physically superlative, and extreme planetary environments in the known universe.

55-cancri-e.x: Tidally locked carbon and diamond-rich lava world where dayside surface temperatures exceed 2,500 K under a molten silicate atmosphere.

proxima-centauri-b.x: Closest known extrasolar planet in a habitable zone, orbiting Sol’s nearest stellar neighbor at 4.25 light-years under extreme stellar flare irradiation.

trappist-1-b.x: Innermost rocky world of the ultra-compact TRAPPIST-1 resonant chain, receiving four times more stellar flux than Earth and confirmed by JWST MIRI to lack a thick atmosphere.

beta-pictoris-b.x: Young, massive super-Jupiter embedded in a massive debris disk, completing an entire rotation in just 8.1 hours (equatorial speed ~100,000 km/h).

europa.x: Smooth ice-covered Jovian moon containing twice the liquid water of all Earth’s oceans combined beneath a 15–25 km ice shell, target of Europa Clipper.

b.s: Catalog of astronomical record-holders: hottest, nearest, densest, youngest, and most biologically promising worlds.
